summary: Validated requested backend and mobile-web frontend scope for optimistic stage update, photo auto-purge >3 days, timeline click-only progression, orderSync queue persistence, and employee dashboard visual behavior.

ui_bugs.issue: Express marker is not red and does not render explicit uppercase 'EXPRESS' label. Observed section text '⚡ Express' with color rgb(30, 26, 52).

integration_issues.issue: flushOrderSync() breaks on first failed POST and only keeps that failed job, dropping subsequent queued jobs. This violates background retry reliability after connectivity recovery.

action_items: Frontend: update Express visual treatment to red accent + explicit EXPRESS label when order.express=true.
Frontend: fix orderSync flush logic to preserve all remaining jobs after first failure and retry full queue on next flush.
Optional hardening: support EXPO_BACKEND_URL fallback in frontend/src/api.ts to match environment contract.
Keep QRIS settlement out-of-scope in this task because it is MOCKED.
critical_code_review_comments: frontend/src/orderSync.ts line 12-13 causes queue truncation after first failed request (data-loss risk for later pending stage updates).
frontend/src/api.ts uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL only; deployment contract requests EXPO_BACKEND_URL usage/fallback.
frontend/app/proses/[id].tsx has next-stage click behavior aligned with optimistic update pattern; non-next stage remained blocked in test.

success_rate.frontend: 83% (core timeline/orderSync load checks passed; Express visual requirement failed)

rca_of_issue: Express visual mismatch RCA: OrdersPipeline renders section title as '⚡ Express' with default dark text and card express border uses brandPrimary (blue), but requirement asks red EXPRESS emphasis. Queue reliability RCA: flushOrderSync() catches first request failure then break; pending array stores only failed job and discards unprocessed tail, so offline bursts can lose queued updates.
